items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I didn't make any money until Kool asked me to give the name Newport up. They paid me.

ctx.x: Did you ever make money in Nice?
Oh yeah, we had some good years. Because we sold all the groups. That kept me alive for awhile 'cause we weren't making much money. In the '80s, remember I was fighting in New

York; we were trying to make it, but we were in business. I had a big business at that time. And I was making a decent year's pay. I wasn't getting ahead of the game; I mean, I'd make $100,000 a year and employing a lot of people, but we worked very hard for it, and I didn't make any money until Kool asked me to give the name Newport up. They paid me. That's the first time I could buy a painting with my money. That was the best thing I ever did was buy paintings, 'cause I made more money from my paintings than I…
